content_html:
Mind awake, body asleep — binaural-beat synthesis and analysis engine.

An open-source engine for the territory Robert Monroe mapped — from his expired patents and our own spectral analysis of the classic gateway-era programs.

Farfield renders layered binaural-beat sessions from plain YAML descriptions, and ships the measurement pipeline its presets were built with. It exists for personal experimentation and research: render your own custom meditation sessions and have fun with it.

What it does

  • Layered sessions: multiple simultaneous carrier pairs with scheduled beat frequencies, phase-coherent segment crossfades, and glide-free seams.
  • Spatial angle modulation (SAM): antiphase sinusoidal phase modulation of a shared carrier — S_L/R(t) = A·sin[2πf_s·t ± φ_p·sin(2πf_m·t)] — which produces a 40 Hz beat percept where a conventional binaural pair won't fuse. See docs/monroe-sound-science.md for the math and the detector that verifies it.
  • Noise beds: pink/brown noise with slow amplitude modulation ("surf"), stereo decorrelation, and band-limited moving textures.
  • An analysis pipeline (farfield.analysis): coherent FFTs, envelope demodulation, and mid/side complex projection that separates true phase modulation from amplitude panning. It measures carriers, beat rates, modulation depths and layer timelines from any stereo recording — it's how the measured presets were made, and how the test suite verifies every render against its numbers.
  • 16 bundled presets (in presets/) in four provenance groups, strongest first: measured from the original tapes, measured from the MSS remasters, from the patents, and original designs. The measurement data behind the first two groups is published in docs/tape-analysis/.

The measured presets were reverse engineered by spectral analysis of personal copies of the classic gateway-era recordings and their modern remasters; the rest implement techniques from the now-public-domain patents (US 3,884,218; US 5,213,562; US 5,356,368) and their abandoned SAM successors. No audio from any recording is included or reproduced — presets are measured numbers, re-synthesized from scratch.

Quick start

Requires Python ≥ 3.11.

git clone https://github.com/txus/farfield && cd farfield

# run straight from the repo with uv, no install:
uv run farfield render presets/focus-10.yaml

# or install the CLI on your PATH:
uv tool install .    # with uv
pip install .        # with plain pip
farfield render presets/focus-10.yaml

Usage

farfield list                          # list the presets in ./presets
farfield list path/to/dir              # or in any directory
farfield render presets/focus-10.yaml  # render a session to WAV
farfield describe presets/focus-10-mss.yaml   # print a session timeline
farfield plot presets/focus-10-mss.yaml       # self-contained HTML visualizer

The CLI takes plain paths — sessions are YAML files, and the bundled presets in presets/ are ordinary examples of them, not a registry. Renders get an 8 s fade-in/out (--fade 0 disables), --seed makes them reproducible, and --json writes a sidecar describing every layer.

Roadmap

  • Layered sessions — stacked carrier pairs, mono anchors, per-ear polarity, beat and carrier glides
  • Spatial angle modulation (SAM) — with closed, open and discontinuous paths
  • Same-ear tremolo — independent rate and depth per ear
  • Shaped noise beds — two-slope spectra, two-stream crossfade panning, fixed interaural delay
  • Moving band-limited textures — the MSS-era "3D" shimmer
  • Quadrature surf — common-mode swell locked to the texture pan
  • Phase-coherent crossfades — click-free seams, verified per render
  • Measurement pipeline — carriers, beats, modulation depths and layer timelines from any stereo recording
  • Isochronic tones — first-class pulsed (gated) tones; the technique most requested in the wider community, including in Tom Campbell's freely published audio experiments
  • Monaural beats — both members summed pre-pan into both ears
  • Carrier FM — per-group LFO on carrier frequency
  • Arbitrary SAM spatial paths — any periodic azimuth trajectory θ(t) via ITD(θ) = (d/c)·sin θ
  • Real-time streaming output — render to an audio device instead of a file

License

  • Code and presets: Apache License 2.0.
  • Measurement data (docs/tape-analysis/*.json): CC0 1.0.
  • Prose docs: CC BY 4.0.

Provenance and trademark details live in NOTICE.

它的作用

  • 分层会话：多个同步载波对，具有预定的拍频、相位相干分段交叉渐变和无滑动接缝。
  • 空间角度调制 (SAM)：共享载波的反相正弦相位调制 — S_L/R(t) = A·sin[2πf_s·t ± φ_p·sin(2πf_m·t)] — 产生 40 Hz 节拍感知，而传统双耳对不会融合。 请参阅 docs/monroe-sound-science.md 了解数学和验证它的检测器。
  • 噪声床：粉红/棕色噪声，具有慢幅度调制（“冲浪”）、立体声去相关和带限移动纹理。
  • 分析管道 (farfield.analysis)：相干 FFT、包络解调以及将真实相位调制与幅度平移分开的中/侧复投影。 它可以测量任何立体声录音的载波、节拍率、调制深度和层时间线——这就是测量预设的制作方式，以及测试套件如何根据其数字验证每个渲染的方式。
  • 16 个捆绑预设（在预设/中）分为四个出处组，最强的第一个：从原始磁带测量、从 MSS 重新制作、从专利和原始设计测量。 前两组背后的测量数据发布在 docs/tape-analysis/ 中。

快速启动

需要 Python ≥ 3.11。

git clone https://github.com/txus/farfield && cd farfield

# run straight from the repo with uv, no install:
uv run farfield render presets/focus-10.yaml

# or install the CLI on your PATH:
uv tool install .    # with uv
pip install .        # with plain pip
farfield render presets/focus-10.yaml

Usage

farfield list                          # list the presets in ./presets
farfield list path/to/dir              # or in any directory
farfield render presets/focus-10.yaml  # render a session to WAV
farfield describe presets/focus-10-mss.yaml   # print a session timeline
farfield plot presets/focus-10-mss.yaml       # self-contained HTML visualizer

CLI 采用简单路径 - 会话是 YAML 文件，预设/中的捆绑预设是它们的普通示例，而不是注册表。 渲染获得 8 秒的淡入/淡出（--fade 0 禁用），--seed 使它们可重现，--json 编写一个描述每一层的 sidecar。

路线图

  • 分层会话 - 堆叠载波对、单声道锚点、每耳极性、节拍和载波滑行
  • 空间角度调制 (SAM) — 具有闭合、开放和不连续路径
  • 同耳颤音 — 每耳独立的速率和深度
  • 成形噪声床 — 双斜率频谱、双流交叉淡入淡出平移、固定耳间延迟
  • 移动带限纹理 — MSS 时代的“3D”微光
  • 正交冲浪 - 共模膨胀锁定到纹理平移
  • 相位相干交叉渐变 — 无点击接缝，每次渲染均经过验证
  • 测量管道 - 来自任何立体声录音的载波、节拍、调制深度和层时间线
  • 等时音 — 一流的脉冲（门控）音；更广泛的社区中最需要的技术，包括汤姆坎贝尔免费发布的音频实验
  • 单耳节拍——两位成员将预声像总结到双耳中
  • Carrier FM — 载波频率上的每组 LFO
  • 任意 SAM 空间路径 — 任何周期性方位轨迹 θ(t) 通过 ITD(θ) = (d/c)·sin θ
  • 实时流输出——渲染到音频设备而不是文件
